factual_notes.source: Microsoft Support: Disk Management in Windows
factual_notes.note: Disk Management is the built-in Windows tool for viewing and managing disks and volumes. Microsoft documents opening it with Start, Search, diskmgmt.msc, or Computer Management.

factual_notes.source: Microsoft Support: Disk Management in Windows
factual_notes.note: Microsoft warns that formatting a volume destroys its data; initialization and new-volume steps are appropriate only for the correctly identified new disk.

factual_notes.source: Microsoft Learn: Change a drive letter
factual_notes.note: An existing volume can receive a letter through Disk Management > Change Drive Letter and Paths > Add, but changing a letter used by Windows or applications can break paths.
Initialization is documented for a new disk with no existing data. Microsoft explicitly warns that initializing a disk already in use erases all data and recommends troubleshooting errors first.

factual_notes.source: Microsoft Support: Safely remove hardware in Windows
factual_notes.note: Microsoft recommends safely ejecting external drives before disconnection to avoid lost or corrupted data.

factual_notes.source: Microsoft Support: Automatically get recommended and updated hardware drivers
factual_notes.note: Windows Update is the supported default source for hardware drivers, includes external drives, and exposes optional driver updates in Windows 11 Advanced options.

factual_notes.source: Microsoft Support: Update drivers through Device Manager in Windows
factual_notes.note: Microsoft documents a targeted device uninstall followed by restart for driver reinstallation and advises using the exact manufacturer rather than nonofficial driver sites.

factual_notes.source: Microsoft Support: Error codes in Device Manager in Windows
factual_notes.note: Device Manager codes distinguish missing, disabled, failed, and driver-loading states; the exact code should be recorded before a code-specific fix is chosen.
